description: Thorny native tree that covers itself in golden scented pompoms in spring. The thorns are the point: they make it one of the safest places in a garden for a small bird to nest.
nativeStatus: Native to central and southern South America
nativeRange: Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Paraguay, Bolivia, southern Brazil
ecology: The signature tree of the espinal. A nitrogen-fixing legume, so it improves the ground around it, and it is hard to kill once established.
wildlifeNotes: The thorny crown is prime nesting habitat, protected from cats and larger predators. The scented flowers are worked hard by bees.
soil: Adaptable; handles poor, dry and salty ground
otherUses: The wood is dense and has long been used for posts and firewood.
safety: The paired thorns are long and sharp. Site it away from paths.
